items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: I’ve got a friend of mine named George Drake, he works with Bill Burham’s office.

ctx.x: You had a quartet with your brother?

Oh yea, the Napoleon Brothers. That was great because we used to go to my mother’s house and we’d fool around at the piano, and my sister used to say, “why don’t you guys get a thing.” So we seriously thought about it. We had the first rehearsal at my mother’s house and man we worked well together. Because we’re both piano players, we’re brothers, but we never played together. So we played some things together, it sounded pretty good. So we said let’s get a group, and we started rehearsing and rehearsing.…

play the big room or the lounge. And we were playing in the lounge and it was open. So now we’re playing on the stand and the bar was long, we were playing over here and the bar went long that way see? So actually we were playing out towards the audience this way and the people are gambling there. So what happened was, we were swinging so hard, that the people started turning around looking at the group and keeping time with their chips, and the dealers were getting bugged.
